title: Rallyboard: Quantified Intent & Mini-Retrospect
content:
Quick context
- Purpose: lightweight, measurable personal habit + outcome log — optimised for 15–30 min weekly digestion. Not another long OKR doc; this is micro-first.
- Timebox: 90-day horizon split into 3x 30-day micro-experiments. Each 30d has a single primary output metric + 1 quality guardrail.

Sprint of life: Feb 20 -> May 20 (30d windows)
- Window A (Feb20–Mar20): Ship baseline autosave demo + reduce blockers in dev environment. Primary metric: 'green-deploy-days' (days with at least one deploy without rollback). Quality guardrail: no regressions that exceed 1-hour incident time-to-detect.
- Window B (Mar21–Apr20): Improve prompt/regression testing coverage for local eval harness. Primary metric: 'prompt-coverage %' on core templates. Guardrail: average eval latency < 300ms for smoke set.
- Window C (Apr21–May20): Personal throughput & learning: complete two deep-dive notebooks on KV-cache and batching heuristics and present to team. Primary metric: 'deep-dive-completions' = 2. Guardrail: presentations < 30 minutes each, include 3 action items.

Why this shape?
- I get distracted by many good projects; forcing one metric per 30d helps tradeoff decisions.
- 'Green-deploy-days' is intentionally coarse — makes success visible without chasing vanity ticks.

Daily micro-routines (minimum viable cadence)
- Morning: 10 min check (what’s the signal? today’s single Most-Important-Task (MIT), blockers).
- Midday: 5–10 min check when there’s context switch — note any interruptions that cost >30min.
- Evening: 10–15 min quick log (did I move the primary metric? 0/1 for the day).
- Weekly: 30 min on Fridays — quick tally + one sentence insight + one experiment for next week.

How I measure (practical rules)
- Binary daily tick for primary metric: 1 = moved forward in an action that plausibly increases the metric (deploy, write test, ship doc, present slide). 0 = otherwise. Keep it blunt to avoid fishing for wins.
- Weekly roll-up: sum of ticks, plus a qualitative note (one-sentence theme).
- Monthly check: compute delta vs baseline and decide whether to continue, pivot, or stop.

Example week (notes, raw)
- Mon: morning — stuck with CI flake, postponed deploy. action: triaged with infra, created linear ticket. tick: 0.
- Tue: small patch landed; 1 green deploy. tick: 1.
- Wed: paired with Lina on smoke tests; added one prompt assert. tick: 1.
- Thu: incident (30m) discovered; mitigated. guardrail flagged but under 1h. tick: 0.
- Fri: retro (30m): week total = 2/5. Theme: 'interruptions upstream'. Next experiment: protect two 90-min focus blocks Tue/Thu.

Mini-retro template (use at each weekly 30m)
1) Theme in one sentence.
2) One number: weekly ticks / expected ticks.
3) Biggest blocker (explicit).
4) One experiment for next week (timeboxed).
5) Confidence check (1–5) on current window continuing.

Examples of experiments (small and testable)
- Calendar lock: 2x90min focus blocks Tue/Thu; make them visible and decline meetings.
- Dev flow: add an autosave PR that runs on PATCH to headless env; measure green-deploy-days increment.
- Guardrail test: add lightweight smoke eval for the top-10 prompts; ensure each PR runs it.

Open questions / unresolved decisions (brain dump)
- What is the right threshold for guardrail latency? 300ms feels arbitrary. Need to sample real-world latency distribution for our smoke set.
- Am I overfitting to deploy frequency as a productivity proxy? Possibly. Consider complementing with code review impact metric (reviews-merged-with-comments>0).
- Where to store the raw daily ticks so that I can compute trends automatically? Options: small sheet (manual), simple markdown file + grep, or lightweight script that writes to a tiny JSON in repo. Preference: tiny repo script (automatable, versioned).

Accountability and social contract
- Weekly sync with Lina (10–15m) — read-only: I share the week tally and one experiment; Lina gives 1–2 suggestions.
- Monthly show-and-tell: short demo to the team to keep momentum and get asymmetric feedback.

Failure modes to watch for
- Gaming the number: counting superficial actions that don’t increase underlying impact. Fix: require paired evidence for each tick (link to PR, screenshot, or one-line result).
- Overload: trying to maintain three active metrics across windows. Fix: drop a window early if engagement <30% for 2 consecutive weeks.
- Analysis paralysis: spending too much time instrumenting rather than shipping. Rule: measure coarse first, refine only if signal justifies it.

Notes to self (micro-ideas)
- Consider a weekly 'no context-switch' day where only one area is touched: engineering OR documentation OR learning. Rotate.
- Put the daily tick mechanism in a tiny CLI: `rally tick <window> --evidence <link>` — then weekly summary is `rally summarize`. Low-effort and versioned in dotfiles.
- If the calendar lock experiment works, try making one lock a recurring 'lab hour' visible on team calendar.

Immediate next actions (this week)
- Implement CLI stub in personal repo (2–3h).
- Protect Tue/Thu 90-min blocks and set calendar notes.
- Add a minimal smoke eval run to PR template (pair with Lina for the first pass).

One-sentence sigil (for the top of the weekly note):
"Ship more with simpler signals: one metric, one guardrail, one experiment — repeat."

End of page — keep this lean.

(If this is useful, migrate to confluence after first 30d with cleaned numbers and two slides of lessons.)
